## 

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
```

\## Data

Monthly seasonally adjusted unemployment rates for the US, Oregon, California, Texas, and New York from FRED, January 1976 to the most recent month.

```{r}
unemp_raw <- read_rds("data/unemp_raw.rds")
head(unemp_raw)
```

\## Wrangling

```{r}
unemp <- unemp_raw |>
  rename(unemployment_rate = price) |>
  mutate(region = case_when(
    symbol == "UNRATE" ~ "United States",
    symbol == "ORUR" ~ "Oregon",
    symbol == "CAUR" ~ "California",
    symbol == "TXUR" ~ "Texas",
    symbol == "NYUR" ~ "New York"
  )) |>
  arrange(region, date) |>
  group_by(region) |>
  mutate(
    unemployment_rate = replace(unemployment_rate, date == as.Date("2025-10-01"),
                                unemployment_rate[date == as.Date("2025-09-01")]),
    unemployment_rate_change = unemployment_rate - lag(unemployment_rate)
  ) |>
  ungroup()

unemp_recent <- filter(unemp, date >= as.Date("2015-01-01"))

unemp_summary <- unemp |>
  group_by(region) |>
  summarize(mean_rate = mean(unemployment_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
            min_rate = min(unemployment_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
            max_rate = max(unemployment_rate, na.rm = TRUE))

unemp_recent_summary <- unemp_recent |>
  group_by(region) |>
  summarize(mean_rate = mean(unemployment_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
            min_rate = min(unemployment_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
            max_rate = max(unemployment_rate, na.rm = TRUE))

unemp_no_covid <- filter(unemp, year(date) != 2020)
unemp_top_increases_no_covid <- slice_max(unemp_no_covid, unemployment_rate_change, n = 5)
unemp_top_decreases_no_covid <- slice_min(unemp_no_covid, unemployment_rate_change, n = 5)

kable(unemp_summary, digits = 2, caption = "Mean, min, and max unemployment rate (%) by region, 1976-present")
kable(unemp_recent_summary, digits = 2, caption = "Mean, min, and max unemployment rate (%) by region, 2015-present")
kable(unemp_top_increases_no_covid, digits = 2, caption = "Five largest month-over-month increases, excluding 2020")
kable(unemp_top_decreases_no_covid, digits = 2, caption = "Five largest month-over-month decreases, excluding 2020")
```

\## Visualization

```{r}
ggplot(unemp, aes(x = date, y = unemployment_rate, color = region)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(title = "Unemployment Rate by Region, 1976-Present", x = "Date", y = "Unemployment Rate (%)", color = "Region") +
  theme_minimal()

ggplot(unemp, aes(x = date, y = unemployment_rate)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~ region) +
  labs(title = "Unemployment Rate by Region, 1976-Present", x = "Date", y = "Unemployment Rate (%)") +
  theme_minimal()

ggplot(unemp_summary, aes(x = fct_reorder(region, mean_rate), y = mean_rate)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(title = "Average Unemployment Rate by Region, 1976-Present", x = "Region", y = "Average Unemployment Rate (%)") +
  theme_minimal()

us <- unemp |>
  filter(region == "United States") |>
  select(date, us_rate = unemployment_rate)

states <- unemp |>
  filter(region != "United States") |>
  left_join(us, by = "date") |>
  mutate(diff = unemployment_rate - us_rate)

ggplot(states, aes(x = date, y = diff, color = region)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0) +
  labs(title = "State Unemployment Rate Minus US Rate", x = "Date", y = "Difference (percentage points)", color = "State") +
  theme_minimal()

```

##Reflection

The dplyr part was pretty straightforward once I figured out what went in each blank, since most of it was just renaming, filtering, and grouping. What tripped me up the most was Git, because when I tried to connect my repo to GitHub it said “remote origin already exists” and I had to use git remote set-url to fix it. I also had trouble getting the data to load at first because I hadn’t run the download step that creates the .rds file yet, and I used AI chat help to figure out both of these problems. Now I feel much more comfortable with committing and pushing my work to GitHub.
